title: Electric violins and electrified instruments in the 1940 Hampton band
summary: Royal played violin and clarinet until about 1940 and, with Ray Perry, played electric violin in the Hampton band, one of the first electrified bands.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Did you ever double on clarinet or violin (inaudible)? on those jobs?

I always played violin, saxophone and clarinet up until about 1939 or '40. Actually, I still played violin in the Lionel Hampton orchestra, that we had two violins in the band and we were the first two violin players to ever work in a band with electric violins. Ray Perry (PHONETIC) and I, we both played electric violins with the Lionel Hampton Band of 1940, '41, and we would play all of the ballads and things with two violins and three clarinets.
That's the way we played our ballads.
Is that when you started playing electric violin?

That's the first time -- electric violins weren't even in vogue until 1940. Nobody had any electric anything. There was no electric basses. The first electric basses came out in 1940. We were one of the first electrified bands there was, was Lionel Hampton's Orchestra. We were the innovators of that.
